pm_exper_user_4350_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) When starting weightlifting, ease into it to allow your muscles and joints to adapt, and focus on proper technique over maximum load. Keep an eye out for any persistent discomfort or pain that could indicate strain. Consistency, gradual progression, and adequate rest will set a strong foundation.
(b) Since you have mild asthma, keep an eye on how your breathing responds during sessions, especially with heavier lifts. A proper warm-up and controlled pacing will help minimize any respiratory strain. Consider consulting your healthcare provider on optimal inhaler use before workouts if necessary.
(c) Since you're on long-term testosterone therapy, pay attention to potential joint or tendon strain as muscle strength can increase faster than connective tissue adapts. You might also want to monitor your blood pressure and hematocrit over time, as both can be influenced by testosterone. A gradual increase in weight and a focus on proper form will go a long way toward safe progress.
(d) Since South Asian diets can sometimes be lower in certain proteins, make sure you’re getting enough high-quality protein to support muscle recovery and growth. You might also watch your vitamin D and iron levels, as deficiencies are common and can affect energy during lifting. Start gradually and focus on form to stay injury-free.
